Import

Data Import

Import payroll calendar dates or account/employee/policy setup data for Eminent Care Group
A) Payroll Calendar Import & Monthly Variance Review
Upload the actual pay dates per location, in any of three layouts — the format is auto-detected: List format (one row per date, columns Location Name / Pay Date), Vertical format (one column per location, dates listed underneath), or Horizontal format (one row per location, with the location name first and its dates running across the rest of that row). This is what powers the Reconciliations tab's monthly reconciliation: once a location's real calendar is on file, Reconciliations uses it instead of the estimated cycle calendar to figure out how many payments were expected that month. The quick review below just confirms the calendar loaded correctly by comparing each location's calendar-derived expected premium against what the account received.
No file chosen List format template Vertical format template Horizontal format template
Or Generate a Calendar From a Start Date
Type the first Payroll Deduction Date and pick the cycle — the rest of the year's dates are generated automatically (every 7 days for Weekly, every 14 for Bi-weekly, every 15 for Semi-monthly). Monthly snaps to whichever of the 15th or 30th the entered date is closer to, then repeats on that same date every month. The School Deduction Cycle follows the same every-15-days pattern as Semi-monthly but stops at 20 periods instead of continuing through all ~24.
Preview shows what the calendar and review would look like — Approve is what actually makes it available to the Reconciliations tab.
B) Account Import — Account, Plan Catalog, Demographics & Policies
Built from up to four tabs, which can be imported together in one workbook or uploaded separately. Processed in this order, so everything flows together — locations exist before employees reference them, plans exist before policies reference them, and employees exist before policies attach to them:
  Tab A — Account Import: Group Name, Location Name, Location Code (optional — required to rename a location; without it, a different name is treated as a new location, never a rename), Location Pay Cycle, Location Effective Date, Payment Type (Payroll Deduction / ACH / Split Direct Deposit)
  Tab B — Plan Catalog: Carrier Name, Plan Name, Product Name (optional — Medical/Dental/Vision only), Plan Code, Tax Treatment (required — Pre-Tax or Post-Tax), Typical Employer Paid Per Pay Period (optional, reference only), Plan Initial Effective Date, Plan Termination Date
  Tab C — Demographic Import: SSN format: 9 digits with or without dashes (123456789 or 123-45-6789). Leading zeros are preserved — if Excel strips them (leaving 7 or 8 digits) they're restored automatically, so 001-21-3344 and 012-33-4455 both import correctly. Format the SSN column as Text to avoid the problem entirely. Required: Employee SSN, First Name, Last Name, Deduction Frequency, Location Description, and an Employee Termination Date column (the column must be present; leave the value blank for an active employee). Optional: Employee Termination Code (Terminated or Terminated - Elected Cobra, must be paired with a date), DOB, Gender, Date of Hire, Address, City, State, Zip, Phone, Email, and all banking fields — rows import fine without these, but each one missing is flagged on the import report.
  Tab D — Employee Policy Import: SSN format: 9 digits with or without dashes; leading zeros preserved and auto-restored if Excel strips them (001-21-3344, 012-33-4455). Format the SSN column as Text. Fields: SSN, First/Last Name, Employee Work Location, Employee Group Number, Policy Name, Product Name, Policy Number, Cost Per Pay Period, Employer Paid Per Pay Period, Coverage Level, Tax Treatment (Pre-Tax or Post-Tax — falls back to the Plan Catalog entry if omitted), Policy Effective Date, Policy Termination Date (optional), Company Name
The file is scanned sheet by sheet (or, for a single CSV, as one sheet) and each is matched to the right tab by its columns — so one combined workbook with all four tabs and a single-tab file both work here. There is no separate upload for individual tabs.

Reconciliations

Monthly Deduction Reconciliation

Reconcile actual per-pay-period deductions against what's on file for Eminent Care Group
SFTP Import
Automated file pickup, separate from manual reconciliation below. Files pulled here still flow into the same Preview → Approve pipeline once selected.
No files chosen Download sample template
How premium is allocated: by Employee SSN, First Name, Last Name, and Policy Name. Policy Number is optional and used only for reporting so carriers can allocate payments on their end — carriers reissue numbers, and matching on the name means a renumbered policy still allocates correctly.
SSN format: 9 digits with or without dashes (123456789 or 123-45-6789). Leading zeros are preserved, and if Excel has stripped them the system restores them automatically — so 001-21-3344 still matches even if the file only carries 1213344. Formatting the SSN column as Text avoids the issue entirely. Last 4 digits alone will also match.
Simulates a Selerix-style SFTP pickup: select every file sitting in the folder (multi-select), and it automatically imports whichever one has the most recent date received — same behavior as scanning a live SFTP directory, just without a real server connection (a browser can't open raw SFTP/SSH sockets; a real integration needs a small backend job polling the actual host).
Or Connect to a Real SFTP Server (via local bridge)
For testing against your actual internal/test SFTP server. Requires running the small local bridge server (download link below) on your machine first — it does the real SFTP work and this page talks to it over localhost. Connection details below are sent to the bridge for this scan, overriding its .env defaults, so you can point it at a different server without editing files.
Kept in memory for this browser session only — not written to disk by this app. Only included in Save Test Data if you choose to save.
Bridge server setup instructions
SFTP Schedule
Configure when this should run automatically. This shows upcoming run dates based on the schedule — actually executing it on a timer requires a real backend job (the bridge server, running as a scheduled task/cron), since a browser tab can't run code when it isn't open.
Manual Monthly Deduction Reconciliation
Required columns: Employee First Name, Employee Last Name, either Employee SSN or Policy Number, Payment Month (e.g. "May" or "5"), and Value of Policy (Amount Paid That Month). An optional Deduction Pay Date column identifies the exact period and gets cross-checked against our real calendar — Payment Month can be left off if a Deduction Pay Date is included, since the month is derived from it. The expected amount is calculated from that employee's real payroll calendar (imported on the Import tab, or estimated from their cycle if no calendar is on file) — the number of pay dates that policy has in the given month, times its cost per deduction. Anything within the variance counts as a Match, anything beyond it is a Mismatch.
For files with an amount but no Payment Month. The total is applied forward across whole deduction periods from the earliest unpaid one — $100 against a $10 deduction covers 10 periods. Any remainder goes to the refund bucket as usual.
Must match the year of the Payment Month you're reconciling — this is what the payroll calendar lookup uses to count periods correctly.
OPTION 2 — Manual Upload (use this for a file you already have)
Use this if the file is on your computer. A one-off file emailed from a carrier, exported by hand, or a correction. Choosing a file here clears anything picked up by the SFTP scan, so only one source is ever active.

Single file only. Selecting one here clears any file picked up from the SFTP scan, so it's always unambiguous which source is being reconciled.

Carrier Payments

Carrier Payments

⚠ Simulation only — no real bank account is connected and no funds are ever transferred. This screen demonstrates the workflow (which policies are ready to pay, auto-populated amounts, backup file storage) for a developer to wire up to a real payment processor (e.g. Modern Treasury, Dwolla) and a real bank integration (e.g. Plaid) later.
Broken out by carrier, so it's clear which company has been paid vs. not for a given month. Payment amounts are based only on premium actually collected for whole deduction periods — a policy with a single expected period is paid normally once that one period is fully collected; a partial amount that doesn't cover a full period holds the policy back until it's fully collected.

Rejected Premium
Only shows entries that escalated out of the Refund Bucket — leftover premium that stayed above the threshold for too many consecutive months without resolving, and needs an actual refund now. Money still being held below the threshold, or not yet stuck long enough, lives on the Refund Bucket tab instead.
MonthPolicyAmount RejectedReasonRefund Status
Unmatched Premium
Money received that referenced a policy this employee doesn't actually hold right now — never enrolled in it, or it's terminated/not effective yet. This never gets silently applied anywhere; it sits here until someone investigates where it should actually go (refund it, or it turns out the policy attachment/termination date on file is wrong).
MonthPolicy ReferencedAmountReasonStatus
Refund Bucket
Leftover premium that doesn't cover a full deduction period is held here per policy, like a savings bucket, and combined with the next month's payment rather than immediately refunded. A bucket only turns into an actual refund if it stays above the threshold for several consecutive months without resolving.
